description:
crl.rs:544-548 — verify_delta_crl_and_collect() ends with:

    Ok(delta_crl.tbs_cert_list.revoked_certificates
        .clone()
        .unwrap_or_default())

This clones the entire Vec<RevokedCert> to return an owned Vec. The CertificateList is borrowed for the duration of the function; returning a reference instead of cloning would eliminate the allocation. Signature change: return &[RevokedCert] borrowed from the parsed CertificateList, which must be kept alive by the caller. Callers (check_revocation, check_revocation_against_anchor) already hold the parsed delta_crl in scope, so lifetime extension is straightforward.

Also, the else-branch Vec::new() at crl.rs:322 and crl.rs:428 is idiomatic given Vec::new() does not heap-allocate, but with a &[RevokedCert] return type both branches become zero-cost.

Priority P3 — correctness unaffected; idiomatic Rust prefers borrowing over cloning when the owner is in scope.
title: [rusty/pkix-revocation] borrow delta entries instead of cloning into Vec
